- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 20–30% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast by 10–20% after 5–7 days of negative sentiment.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is > 2.5x recent 18-day average, apply a 50% decay rule to correct for overconfidence.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 0.5x historical mean, model is underestimating; add 0.1–0.2 to forecast for next 3 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
